Main.sentence: George Herbert Walker Bush [a] (June 12, 1924 – November 30, 2018) was the 41st ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , serving from 1989 to 1993. A member of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , he also served as the 43rd ___E:vice president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States)___ under President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ from 1981 to 1989 and previously in various other ___E:federal positions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States)___ .

Born into ___E:a wealthy, established family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_family)___ in ___E:Milton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Massachusetts)___ , Bush was raised in ___E:Greenwich, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich,_Connecticut)___ .

He attended ___E:Phillips Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_Academy)___ and served as a pilot in the ___E:United States Navy Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Reserve)___ during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ before graduating from ___E:Yale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University)___ and moving to ___E:West Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Texas)___ , where he established oil company ___E:Zapata Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HRG_Group)___ .

Following an unsuccessful run for the United States Senate ___E:in 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas)___ , he was elected to represent ___E:Texas's 7th congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas%27s_7th_congressional_district)___ in 1966. President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ appointed Bush as the ___E:ambassador to the United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_the_United_Nations)___ in 1971 and as ___E:chairman of the Republican National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Republican_National_Committee)___ in 1973. President ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ appointed him as the ___E:chief of the Liaison Office to the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_the_Liaison_Office_to_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ in 1974 and as the ___E:director of Central Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_Central_Intelligence)___ in 1976. Bush ran for president in 1980 but was defeated in the ___E:Republican presidential primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ by Reagan, who then selected Bush as his vice presidential running mate. In the ___E:1988 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Bush defeated Democrat ___E:Michael Dukakis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Dukakis)___ .

Foreign policy drove ___E:Bush's presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_George_H._W._Bush)___ as he navigated the final years of the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ and played a key role in the ___E:reunification of Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reunification_of_Germany)___ .

He presided over the ___E:invasion of Panama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Panama)___ and the ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ , ending the ___E:Iraqi occupation of Kuwait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_occupation_of_Kuwait)___ in the latter conflict.

Though the agreement was not ratified until after he left office, Bush negotiated and signed the ___E:North American Free Trade Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Free_Trade_Agreement)___ , which created a trade bloc consisting of the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Domestically, Bush reneged on ___E:a 1988 campaign promise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read_my_lips:_no_new_taxes)___ by enacting legislation to raise taxes that he justified as necessary to reducing the budget deficit.

He championed and signed three pieces of bipartisan legislation in 1990, the ___E:Americans with Disabilities Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_with_Disabilities_Act)___ , the ___E:Immigration Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_Act_of_1990)___ and the ___E:Clean Air Act Amendments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Air_Act_Amendments)___ .
He also appointed ___E:David Souter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Souter)___ and ___E:Clarence Thomas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_Thomas)___ to the Supreme Court.

Bush lost the ___E:1992 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_presidential_election)___ to Democrat ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ following ___E:an economic recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_1990s_recession)___ , his turnaround on his tax promise, and the decreased emphasis of foreign policy in a post–Cold War political climate.
After leaving office in 1993, Bush was active in humanitarian activities, often working alongside Clinton.

With the victory of his eldest son, ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ , in the ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ and ___E:2004 presidential elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election)___ , the two became the second father–son pair to serve as the nation's president, following ___E:John Adams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Adams)___ and ___E:John Quincy Adams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams)___ .

His second son, ___E:Jeb Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Bush)___ , unsuccessfully sought the Republican presidential nomination in the ___E:2016 primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ . ___E:Historians generally rank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ Bush as an above-average president.
George Herbert Walker Bush was born on June 12, 1924, in ___E:Milton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Massachusetts)___ .

He was the second son of ___E:Prescott Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescott_Bush)___ and ___E:Dorothy (née Walker) Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Wear_Walker_Bush)___ ,  and a younger brother of ___E:Prescott Bush Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescott_Bush_Jr.)___ His paternal grandfather, ___E:Samuel P. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_P._Bush)___ , worked as an executive for a railroad parts company in ___E:Columbus, Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio)___ ,  while his maternal grandfather and namesake, ___E:George Herbert Walker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Herbert_Walker)___ , led ___E:Wall Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street)___ investment bank ___E:W. A. Harriman & Co. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._A._Harriman_%26_Co.)___  Walker was known as "Pop", and young Bush was called "Poppy" as a tribute to him.
The Bush family moved to ___E:Greenwich, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich,_Connecticut)___ , in 1925, and Prescott took a position with W. A.

Harriman & Co., which later merged into ___E:Brown Brothers Harriman & Co. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_Brothers_Harriman_%26_Co.)___ the following year.  Bush spent most of his childhood in Greenwich, at the family vacation home in ___E:Kennebunkport, Maine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennebunkport,_Maine)___ , [b] or at his maternal grandparents' plantation in South Carolina.
Because of the family's wealth, Bush was largely unaffected by the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States)___ .

He attended ___E:Greenwich Country Day School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Country_Day_School)___ from 1929 to 1937 and ___E:Phillips Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_Academy)___ , an elite private academy in Massachusetts, from 1937 to 1942.  While at Phillips Academy, he served as president of the senior class, secretary of the student council, president of the community fund-raising group, a member of the editorial board of the school newspaper, and captain of the varsity baseball and soccer teams.

On his 18th birthday, immediately after graduating from Phillips Academy, he enlisted in the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ as a ___E:naval aviator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator_(United_States))___ .

After a period of training, he was commissioned as an ensign in the Naval Reserve at ___E:Naval Air Station Corpus Christi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Corpus_Christi)___ on June 9, 1943, becoming one of the youngest pilots in the Navy.  [c] Beginning in 1944, Bush served in the Pacific theater, where he flew a ___E:Grumman TBM Avenger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_TBM_Avenger)___ , a ___E:torpedo bomber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_bomber)___ capable of taking off from aircraft carriers.

His squadron was assigned to the ___E:USS San Jacinto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_San_Jacinto_(CVL-30))___ as a member of Air Group 51, where his lanky physique earned him the nickname "Skin".

Bush flew his first combat mission in May 1944, bombing Japanese-held ___E:Wake Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Island)___ ,  and was promoted to lieutenant (junior grade) on August 1, 1944. During an attack on a Japanese installation in ___E:Chichijima U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chichijima)___ , Bush's aircraft successfully attacked several targets but was downed by enemy fire.  Though both of Bush's fellow crew members died, Bush successfully bailed out from the aircraft and was rescued by the submarine ___E:USS Finback U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Finback_(SS-230))___ .  [d] Several of the aviators shot down during the attack were captured and executed, and their livers were ___E:cannibalized by their captors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chichijima_incident)___ .

Bush's survival after such a close brush with death shaped him profoundly, leading him to ask, "Why had I been spared and what did God have for me?"  He was later awarded the ___E:Distinguished Flying Cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States))___ for his role in the mission.
Bush returned to San Jacinto in November 1944, participating in operations in the Philippines.
In early 1945, he was assigned to a new combat squadron, VT-153, where he trained to participate in an ___E:invasion of mainland Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Downfall)___ .
Between March and May 1945, he trained in ___E:Auburn, Maine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn,_Maine)___ , where he and Barbara lived in a small apartment.

On September 2, 1945, before any invasion took place, Japan formally surrendered following the ___E:atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_bombings_of_Hiroshima_and_Nagasaki)___ .
Bush was released from active duty that same month but was not formally discharged from the Navy until October 1955, when he had reached the rank of lieutenant.
By the end of his period of active service, Bush had flown 58 missions, completed 128 carrier landings, and recorded 1228 hours of flight time.

Bush met ___E:Barbara Pierce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Bush)___ at a Christmas dance in Greenwich in December 1941,  and, after a period of courtship, they became engaged in December 1943.  While Bush was on leave from the Navy, they married in ___E:Rye, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rye,_New_York)___ , on January 6, 1945.  The Bushes enjoyed a strong marriage, and Barbara would later be a popular First Lady, seen by many as "a kind of national grandmother".  [e] They had six children: ___E:George W. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ (b. 1946), ___E:Robin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Robinson_Bush)___ (1949–1953), ___E:Jeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Bush)___ (b. 1953), ___E:Neil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Bush)___ (b. 1955), ___E:Marvin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Bush)___ (b. 1956), and ___E:Doro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Bush_Koch)___ (b. 1959).
Their oldest daughter, Robin, died of leukemia in 1953.

Bush enrolled at ___E:Yale College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_College)___ , where he took part in an accelerated program that enabled him to graduate in two and a half years rather than the usual four.  He was a member of the ___E:Delta Kappa Epsilon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Kappa_Epsilon)___ fraternity and was elected its president.
He also captained the Yale baseball team and played in the first two ___E:College World Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_World_Series)___ as a left-handed first baseman.
Like his father, he was a member of the Yale cheerleading squad  and was initiated into the ___E:Skull and Bones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_and_Bones)___ secret society.
He graduated ___E:Phi Beta Kappa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa)___ in 1948 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics.
After graduating from Yale, Bush moved his young family to ___E:West Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Texas)___ .

Biographer Jon Meacham writes that Bush's relocation to Texas allowed him to move out of the "daily shadow of his Wall Street father and Grandfather Walker, two dominant figures in the financial world," but would still allow Bush to "call on their connections if he needed to raise capital."  His first position in Texas was an ___E:oil field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_field)___ equipment salesman  for ___E:Dresser Industries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dresser_Industries)___ , which was led by family friend Neil Mallon.

While working for Dresser, Bush lived in various places with his family: ___E:Odessa, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odessa,_Texas)___ ; ___E:Ventura U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura,_California)___ , ___E:Bakersfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakersfield,_California)___ and ___E:Compton, California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compton,_California)___ ; and ___E:Midland, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midland,_Texas)___ .

In 1952, he volunteered for the successful presidential campaign of ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_(United_States))___ candidate ___E:Dwight D. Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ .
That same year, his father won election to represent Connecticut in the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ as a member of the Republican Party.

With support from Mallon and Bush's uncle, ___E:George Herbert Walker Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Herbert_Walker_Jr.)___ , Bush and John Overbey launched the Bush-Overbey Oil Development Company in 1951.  In 1953, he co-founded the ___E:Zapata Petroleum Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HRG_Group)___ , an oil company that drilled in the ___E:Permian Basin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian_Basin_(North_America))___ in Texas.
In 1954, he was named president of the Zapata Offshore Company, a subsidiary which specialized in ___E:offshore drilling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_drilling)___ .
Shortly after the subsidiary became independent in 1959, Bush moved the company and his family from Midland to ___E:Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston)___ .

There, he befriended ___E:James Baker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Baker)___ , a prominent attorney who later became an important political ally.  Bush remained involved with Zapata until the mid-1960s, when he sold his stock in the company for approximately $1 million.

In 1988, The Nation published an article alleging that Bush worked as an operative of the ___E:Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ (CIA) during the 1960s; Bush denied this claim.

By the early 1960s, Bush was widely regarded as an appealing political candidate, and some leading ___E:Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ attempted to convince Bush to become a Democrat.
He declined to leave the Republican Party, later citing his belief that the national Democratic Party favored "big, centralized government".

The Democratic Party had historically dominated Texas, but Republicans scored their first major victory in the state with ___E:John G. Tower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_G._Tower)___ 's victory in a 1961 special election to the United States Senate.

Motivated by Tower's victory and hoping to prevent the far-right ___E:John Birch Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Birch_Society)___ from coming to power, Bush ran for the chairmanship of the ___E:Harris County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris_County,_Texas)___ Republican Party, winning election in February 1963.  Like most other Texas Republicans, Bush supported conservative Senator ___E:Barry Goldwater U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Goldwater)___ over the more centrist ___E:Nelson Rockefeller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Rockefeller)___ in the ___E:1964 Republican Party presidential primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ .

In 1964, Bush sought to unseat liberal Democrat ___E:Ralph W. Yarborough U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_W._Yarborough)___ in ___E:Texas's U.S. Senate election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas)___ .

Bolstered by superior fundraising, Bush won the Republican primary by defeating former gubernatorial nominee ___E:Jack Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Cox_(Texas_politician))___ in a ___E:run-off election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run-off_election)___ .

In the general election, Bush attacked Yarborough's vote for the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964)___ , which banned racial and gender discrimination in public institutions and many privately owned businesses.

Bush argued that the act unconstitutionally expanded the federal government's powers, but he was privately uncomfortable with the racial politics of opposing the act.  He lost the election 56 percent to 44 percent, though he did run well ahead of Barry Goldwater, the Republican presidential nominee.

Despite the loss, The New York Times reported that Bush was "rated by political friend and foe alike as the Republicans' best prospect in Texas because of his attractive personal qualities and the strong campaign he put up for the Senate".

In ___E:1966 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)___ , Bush ran for the ___E:United States House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ in ___E:Texas's 7th congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas%27s_7th_congressional_district)___ , a newly redistricted seat in the ___E:Greater Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Houston)___ area. Initial polling showed him trailing his Democratic opponent, Harris County District Attorney Frank Briscoe, but he ultimately won the race with 57 percent of the vote.  To woo potential candidates in the South and Southwest, House Republicans secured Bush an appointment to the powerful ___E:United States House Committee on Ways and Means U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Ways_and_Means)___ , making Bush the first freshman to serve on the committee since 1904.  His voting record in the House was generally ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States)___ .

He supported the ___E:Nixon administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Richard_Nixon)___ 's ___E:Vietnam policies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamization)___ but broke with Republicans on the issue of ___E:birth control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_control)___ , which he supported.
He also voted for the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1968 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1968)___ , although it was generally unpopular in his district.

In 1968, Bush joined several other Republicans in issuing the party's ___E:Response to the State of the Union address U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Response_to_the_State_of_the_Union_address)___ ; Bush's part of the address focused on a call for fiscal responsibility.

Though most other Texas Republicans supported ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ in the ___E:1968 Republican Party presidential primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ , Bush endorsed ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ , who went on to win the party's nomination.

Nixon considered selecting Bush as his running mate in the ___E:1968 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_United_States_presidential_election)___ , but he ultimately chose ___E:Spiro Agnew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew)___ instead.
Bush won re-election to the House unopposed, while Nixon defeated ___E:Hubert Humphrey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey)___ in the presidential election.

In 1970, with President Nixon's support, Bush gave up his seat in the House to ___E:run for the Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas)___ against Yarborough.
Bush easily won the Republican primary, but Yarborough was defeated by the more centrist ___E:Lloyd Bentsen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Bentsen)___ in the Democratic primary.
Ultimately, Bentsen defeated Bush, taking 53.5 percent of the vote.

After the 1970 Senate election, Bush accepted a position as a senior adviser to the president, but he convinced Nixon to instead appoint him as the ___E:U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Ambassador_to_the_United_Nations)___ .

The position represented Bush's first foray into foreign policy, as well as his first major experiences with the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ and China, the two major U.S. rivals in the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ .
During Bush's tenure, the Nixon administration pursued a policy of détente, seeking to ease tensions with both the Soviet Union and China.

Bush's ambassadorship was marked by a defeat on the China question, as the ___E:United Nations General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly)___ voted, in ___E:Resolution 2758 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resolution_2758)___ , to expel the ___E:Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China)___ and replace it with the People's Republic of China in October 1971.  In the ___E:1971 crisis in Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Pakistani_War_of_1971)___ , Bush supported an Indian motion at the UN General Assembly to condemn the Pakistani government of ___E:Yahya Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahya_Khan)___ for waging genocide in ___E:East Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Pakistan)___ (modern Bangladesh), referring to the "tradition which we have supported that the human rights question transcended domestic jurisdiction and should be freely debated".

Bush's support for India at the UN put him into conflict with Nixon who was supporting Pakistan, partly because Yahya Khan was a useful intermediary in his attempts to reach out to China and partly because the president was fond of Yahya Khan.
